title: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing
name: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing
metaTitle: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing in Dallas, TX
metaDescription: Net-lease and single-tenant sourcing for Dallas 1031 exchanges: pad sites, corridor stock, lease credit review, and 45-day identification timing.

sections.html:
Net-lease and single-tenant properties are the asset class most exchange investors reach for when they want to stop managing something day to day. Dallas has deep pad-site and freestanding-building inventory along its major corridors, which makes the search easier than in a thin secondary market, but it also means the identification letter needs to be locked before the better sites get pulled off market.

That depth cuts both ways: more inventory means more choices, but it also means more competing buyers moving on the same short list of well-located corners the day they list, so speed matters as much as selection.

sections.heading: Where Net-Lease Stock Runs Deepest
sections.html:
The LBJ Freeway corridor and Preston Road carry a long run of pad sites in front of larger retail centers, occupied by quick-service restaurants, banks, and auto-parts stores. Northwest Highway and the Loop 12 frontage have older freestanding buildings, some built for drugstores and now backfilled with regional operators after a lease turnover.

Further north, the corridors feeding into Addison and Carrollton carry newer construction with longer initial lease terms, since much of that development happened alongside more recent retail buildout rather than being retrofitted from an older shopping center outparcel.

sections.heading: Corporate Credit vs Franchisee Guarantees
sections.html:
The lease guarantee matters as much as the real estate. A corporate-guaranteed lease behind a national brand underwrites very differently than the same building leased to a single-unit franchisee whose personal guarantee is the only backstop. We pull the guarantor structure before anything goes on a candidate list, because that distinction affects both loan terms and resale value years down the road.

A multi-unit franchisee operating a dozen locations across the metro carries a different risk profile than a single-location operator whose entire business is tied to the one building on the candidate list, and lenders price that difference into the loan terms whether or not a buyer notices it upfront.

sections.heading: Reading the Lease Beyond the Rent Number
sections.html:
Rent escalations, renewal option counts, and who's responsible for roof and structure are the details that separate a clean net-lease asset from one that looks clean on a one-page summary. A lease with flat rent for fifteen years and no scheduled bumps is a different hold than one with 10 percent escalations every five years, even at the same starting cap rate.

Roof and structure responsibility deserves its own line of scrutiny, since some net-lease agreements labeled absolute triple net still carve out landlord responsibility for the roof membrane or foundation, which changes the true passivity of the investment considerably.

sections.heading: What Every Candidate Clears Before It Reaches You
sections.html:
Before a net-lease or single-tenant property lands on a client's identification letter, it goes through a fixed pass that looks past the corridor average to the specific corner:

  • Guarantor structure and corporate versus franchisee backing
  • Remaining primary lease term against the investor's hold horizon
  • Landlord versus tenant responsibility for roof, structure, and parking lot repairs
  • Traffic count and access at the specific corner
  • Any co-tenancy or exclusive-use clause tied to a neighboring center

A corridor with strong average traffic counts can still hide a weak individual corner if access is awkward or a curb cut was closed years ago, so we look at the site itself before trusting a broker's corridor-level summary.

sections.heading: Timing the Purchase to Your Exchange Deadlines
sections.html:
Net-lease closings can move faster than any other asset class since there's usually a single tenant and a simple title picture, which is useful when a client is racing the 180-day exchange period after a slow identification process. We still route every dollar through your qualified intermediary so the transaction stays inside the exchange structure and no proceeds pass through your hands directly.

That speed makes net-lease a common backup candidate on a three-property identification letter even when the investor's primary target is a slower-moving multifamily or industrial deal.

faqs.q: What's the practical difference between an NNN and an STNL property?
faqs.a: The terms overlap heavily in everyday use. NNN describes the lease structure where the tenant pays taxes, insurance, and maintenance, while STNL simply means a single tenant occupies the whole building. Most Dallas net-lease pad sites are both at once.

faqs.q: Is a franchisee-guaranteed lease disqualifying for an exchange?
faqs.a: No, it doesn't affect like-kind treatment at all. It affects underwriting and financing terms, since a franchisee guarantee carries more credit risk than a corporate guarantee behind the same brand name.

faqs.q: How quickly can a net-lease closing happen once it's identified?
faqs.a: Often faster than multifamily or industrial, since the title and lease picture is usually simple. That speed is useful when the 45-day identification period has already used up most of the runway before the 180-day exchange deadline.

faqs.q: Do rent escalations matter for exchange purposes?
faqs.a: Not for the like-kind test, but they matter enormously for the investment itself. A flat-rent lease with no bumps for over a decade is a materially different hold than one with regular scheduled increases at the same starting price.

faqs.q: Can a single-tenant building with a short remaining lease term still work as replacement property?
faqs.a: It can qualify, but a short remaining term usually means weaker financing terms and more re-leasing risk at renewal. We flag remaining term length early so an investor isn't surprised by it after the identification letter is already filed, and we price that risk into the offer rather than glossing over it.
